cases.scope: The upper-ontology terms Noesis declares itself (SPEC §3, §12.6): the agent classes, the fluent vocabulary, the single principal, and the one datatype minted where XSD has no counterpart.
cases.authority: This project. `dev.librecybernetics.noesis.vocab.CoreModule` and `dev.librecybernetics.noesis.logic.Vocab` are the registers of record; a term exists when one of them declares it.
cases.semantic: A class name denotes the object class itself. A property name denotes a property of its domain class and reads subject-first, so that `{s} {property} {o}` verbalizes. Nothing in a name records where a term came from or how it is stored.
cases.syntactic: One name part per term, no separators, no qualifier terms except where a qualifier precedes what it qualifies (`timeVarying`, `partialDate`).
cases.lexical: ASCII letters and digits, English, no abbreviations. UpperCamelCase for classes; lowerCamelCase for properties, individuals and datatypes.
cases.uniqueness: One item per name and one name per item (§8.1.2): no homonyms and no synonyms within the namespace. Agreement with a term in another namespace is expressed by an equivalence axiom, never by reusing its name.

cases.scope: The relationship vocabulary of SPEC §7: agents, the ties between them, interactions and life events, and the Name objects of §7.2.
cases.authority: This project. `dev.librecybernetics.noesis.vocab.RelationshipsModule` is the register of record.
cases.semantic: A property name states the relation as the subject holds it (`worksAt`, `parentOf`), so its inverse is a separate term rather than a reading of the same one. Names carry no cardinality, gender or arity assumption, which is why `partnerOf` and `parentOf` are named as they are.
cases.syntactic: One name part per term. A relational property ends in the preposition-derived part that fixes its direction (`Of`, `At`, `To`, `By`).
cases.lexical: ASCII letters and digits, English, no abbreviations. UpperCamelCase for classes; lowerCamelCase for properties.
cases.uniqueness: One item per name and one name per item within the namespace.

cases.scope: The language-learning vocabulary of SPEC §6: concepts, lexemes, word forms and the relations among them.
cases.authority: This project. `dev.librecybernetics.noesis.vocab.LanguageModule` is the register of record.
cases.semantic: A class name denotes a linguistic object; a property name denotes the relation from the hub to a spoke or between two lexical items, read subject-first.
cases.lexical: ASCII letters and digits, English metalanguage even for terms about other languages, no abbreviations. UpperCamelCase for classes; lowerCamelCase for properties.
cases.uniqueness: One item per name and one name per item within the namespace.

cases.scope: The ValueFlows vocabulary as imported by SPEC §8. Descriptive: Noesis records these names, it does not coin them.
cases.authority: The ValueFlows vocabulary (https://valueflo.ws/). Noesis's only contribution in this namespace is the single alignment axiom `vf:Agent ≡ core:Agent`, which adds no name.
cases.semantic: ValueFlows' REA semantics. A name means what the upstream vocabulary says it means; a divergence in meaning is an import bug, not a naming decision.
cases.syntactic: As published upstream: one name part per term.
cases.lexical: As published upstream: UpperCamelCase for classes, lowerCamelCase for properties. Recorded so that a mistyped import fails rather than silently minting a Noesis-local term.
cases.uniqueness: One item per name, inherited from upstream. Synonyms are not introduced locally.

cases.scope: The subset of the FOAF vocabulary used by the mapped RDF interchange boundary in SPEC §7.3. Descriptive: Noesis records these upstream names and does not coin terms in this namespace.
cases.authority: The FOAF Vocabulary Project, FOAF Vocabulary Specification (https://xmlns.com/foaf/spec/). `dev.librecybernetics.noesis.vocab.Foaf` records the subset mapped by Noesis.
cases.semantic: A name means what the upstream FOAF vocabulary specifies. Noesis maps those terms to its canonical PRM model without treating matching names or inverse-functional properties as automatic identity.
cases.syntactic: As published upstream: one name part per term.
cases.lexical: As published upstream: UpperCamelCase for classes and lowerCamelCase for properties. Recorded so that a mistyped adapter term fails rather than silently inventing a local FOAF term.
cases.uniqueness: One item per name, inherited from upstream. Noesis introduces no synonyms in the FOAF namespace.

cases.scope: Reserved for the references and locators of SPEC §3.7 and §9. No term is declared yet; the namespace is bound so that the convention is settled before the first one is.
cases.authority: This project. No register of record exists until the module does.
cases.semantic: A class name will denote a kind of reference or locator; a property name will denote a relation from a reference to its target or its metadata.
cases.lexical: ASCII letters and digits, English, no abbreviations. UpperCamelCase for classes; lowerCamelCase for properties.
cases.uniqueness: One item per name and one name per item within the namespace.

cases.scope: Minted entity identifiers — the individuals capture creates. Vocabulary terms are never named here; that separation is what lets an entity be renamed without touching the ontology.
cases.authority: This project, assigned by `Iri.fresh` rather than by a person. There is no name list to consult.
cases.semantic: None by design. A minted identifier carries no meaning, so that correcting what an entity *is* never invalidates its identifier and no consumer can parse significance out of it.
cases.syntactic: `e/` followed by the identifier: a collection part, a separator, and the identifier part.
cases.lexical: A UUID version 4 (RFC 9562) in lowercase hexadecimal with hyphens.
cases.uniqueness: One item per name, from the UUID. One name per item is *not* asserted: an entity may be found equal to another, and `SameIndividual` records that rather than renaming either.

cases.scope: The RDF 1.1 terms Noesis uses. Descriptive: these names are the W3C's.
cases.authority: W3C, RDF 1.1 Concepts and Abstract Syntax.
cases.syntactic: As published: one name part per term.

cases.scope: The RDF Schema terms Noesis uses. Descriptive.
cases.syntactic: As published: one name part per term.

cases.scope: The XSD 1.1 Part 2 datatypes Noesis mints literals in. Descriptive.
cases.authority: W3C, XML Schema Definition Language 1.1 Part 2: Datatypes.
cases.semantic: As defined by XSD 1.1 Part 2: a name denotes a lexical space, a value space and the mappings between them.
cases.syntactic: As published: one name part per term.
cases.lexical: As published: lowerCamelCase, including the `g` prefix on the Gregorian calendar datatypes.

cases.scope: The W3C Basic Geo (WGS84) terms the place model of SPEC §7 uses. Descriptive: these names are the W3C's, reached through ValueFlows, whose `vf:SpatialThing` extends `geo:SpatialThing`.
cases.authority: W3C, WGS84 Geo Positioning: an RDF vocabulary.
cases.semantic: As defined by Basic Geo: a `SpatialThing` is anything with spatial extent, and the coordinate properties are decimal degrees and metres.
cases.syntactic: As published: one name part per term, except `lat_long`, which joins two.
cases.lexical: As published: UpperCamelCase for classes, lowerCamelCase for properties — with an underscore in `lat_long`, which is why the rule below admits one. Recording that is the point of a descriptive convention: the upstream name is correct by definition, and a rule that forbade it would fail the import rather than the typo.

cases.scope: Bound for OWL-level output. No term is used yet; the binding exists so that Turtle output can declare it when one is.
cases.syntactic: As published: one name part per term.
cases.lexical: As published: UpperCamelCase for classes, lowerCamelCase for properties.
